messages:
marin: FYI i experimented with an alternative "admission credits" surface for dedicated pools. Instead of publishing discrete GPU counts we emit a compact vector of fractional credits (short_gpu, long_gpu, kv) + per-sku efficiency factors. Purpose: reduce wasted prewarm on tiny requests and give routing a clean cost signal. draft: https://redwood.internal/rfc/credits-v2

leo: interesting. how do credits change eviction logic? my worry is mixing fractional signals with existing slot-based preemption could be surprising to ops.

marin: good catch. design constraint: credits are advisory for admission and for "soft" eviction ranking only. we keep the strong preemption path unchanged: reserved_slots and lease tickets still win. credits can only nudge the soft-score within a bounded band.

ara: can you share the scoring sketch? tiny formula helps me reason about fairness.

marin: sure. soft_eviction_score = base_priority + preempt_penalty - alpha * min(effective_credits, credit_cap) + beta * recent_cost_spike. credit_cap is small (e.g., 0.2 of priority range) so credits cannot flip guaranteed-SLA tenants.

sanjay: operational notes: snapshots need seq id + ttl. if stale, admission must ignore credits and fallback to absolute capacity. also we should emit credit_staleness and credit_fallback_count metrics.

ivy: UI ops ask: explain mapping in plain english. i.e., "0.02 short_gpu ~= one quick chat turn". include human-friendly examples in the UI and add a per-pool debug toggle that expands the compact vector into explicit entries.

marin: agreed. will add example mapping and a debug-expanded stream that samples a few rows/minute so SRE can inspect without enabling verbose mode globally.

leo: what about mixed SKUs? we need sku_factor table in each snapshot so credits convert to effective-gpu-units. also add a sku_constraint boolean on credits for model-affinity (A100-only). admission must enforce sku_compatibility when that flag is set.

ara: i'd add a reserved_credit flag per tenant so critical customers don't get soft-scored by credits at all. that should be honored even for admission heuristics.

marin: good point. reserved_credit will be separate from reserved_slots; it simply exempts a tenant from credit-driven scoring.

autoscaler-bot: queued canary: admission-credits-v2 on canary-5 at 2026-04-02T07:00Z. collectors: credit_staleness, eviction_churn_by_cause, p95_tail, credit_fallback_count.

leo: rollout checklist proposal: 1) proto w/ seq+ttl + sku_factors, 2) capped soft-scorer impl, 3) snapshot staleness guards + fallback, 4) debug-expanded minute samples, 5) canary matrix: mostly-small, mixed-large, sudden-burst, 6) rollback if eviction_churn > 3x or p95 > 1.25x baseline.

ara: testing addition: synthetic run where 300 tiny requests start in 2s to confirm spike detector flips to absolute capacity and prevents silent overload. add a durability test where cost estimates flip rapidly to validate no double-accounting in billing.

marin: i'll update the RFC follow-up with proto diffs, scorer pseudo-code, dashboards, and an operator runbook (how to disable credit scoring per pool and how to read the debug samples). tagging @leo @ara @sanjay @ivy for review.

autoscaler-bot: canary started: first 10m window sample - credit_staleness_med=1.3s, eviction_churn=0.7/10m, p95_tail +2.1% vs baseline. dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/credits-v2-canary

marin: nice. closing this thread for now. open a PR for the RFC patch and ping me if you see anything odd in canary metrics.
